, the first official U.S. response to communism during the Cold War.

contents.text: Read the modified excerpt from Truman's speech. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: At the present moment in world history, nearly every country must choose between different ways of life. Too often, people are not allowed to make this choice freely.

One way of life is based on the will of the majority. This way of life is known for having representative government, free elections, promises of individual liberty, freedom of speech and religion, and freedom from political cruelty.

The second way of life is based on the will of a small group being forced upon the majority. This way of life relies on terror and abuse, controls the press and radio, holds unfair elections, and limits people's personal freedoms.

aid. This will help strengthen economies and help keep governments stable.

Under his rule, millions of Soviet citizens starved. Also, millions of people were falsely accused of being traitors and were either imprisoned or executed. By the time World War II began, Stalin had total control of life in the Soviet Union.

During World War II, the Soviet Union was invaded by Nazi Germany. The Soviet Union joined the Allied powers and pushed the German army back, taking over much of Germany and the territory it had controlled in Eastern Europe. By the end of the war, the Soviet army was the largest in the world, and it controlled many Eastern European nations.

Countries can be democratic, which means they have a free and fair political system and guaranteed rights.
Support for free peoples should mainly be through peaceful support, such as money.
Countries can be unfree, which means that their political system is unfair and their people don't have many rights or freedoms.
Now that World War II is over, people have to choose the future of their countries.

staticItems.text: At the present moment in world history, nearly every country must choose between different ways of life. Too often, people are not allowed to make this choice freely.

One way of life is based on the will of the majority, with representative government, free elections, promises of individual liberty, freedom of speech and religion, and freedom from political cruelty.

The second way of life is based on the will of a small group being forced upon the majority. It relies on terror and abuse, controls the press and radio, holds unfair elections, and limits personal freedoms.
I believe that the United States must support free countries who are resisting attempted control by small, armed groups or by other countries.
I believe that our help should be mainly through economic and financial aid. This will help strengthen economies and help keep governments stable.

pieces.text: During the Russian Revolution, the royal family was overthrown and a new, communist government was established. Russia became part of a new country called the Soviet Union. It was the world's first
country. In theory, the goal of communism is for all people to have equal wealth and equal rights. But the Soviet Union did not achieve a peaceful society of equals.

textContent.text: The Soviet government went to extreme measures to transform society, taking control of the economy and severely limiting citizens' personal freedom. Soon after the Soviet Union was formed, Joseph Stalin became its leader and gave key government positions to the people most loyal to him. His government killed his rivals. Under his rule, millions of Soviet citizens starved. Also, millions of people were falsely accused of being traitors and were either imprisoned or executed. By the time World War II began, Stalin had total control of life in the Soviet Union.

During World War II, the Soviet Union was invaded by Nazi Germany. The Soviet Union joined the Allied powers and pushed the German army back, taking over much of Germany and the territory it had controlled in Eastern Europe. By the end of the war, the Soviet army was the largest in the world, and it controlled many Eastern European nations.

contents.text: U.S. soldiers faced difficult conditions in Vietnam. The excerpts below come from interviews with two soldiers about their wartime experiences. Read the excerpts or use the audio button to hear recordings from the interviews. Then answer the question below.

pieces.text: Guadalupe Carrasco was drafted into the army and served in a light infantry unit during the war. He earned a Purple Heart award for his service.

content.text: The North Vietnamese Army—they were a regular army, and you knew that they were the enemy. Now the Viet Cong, on the other hand, are farmers during the day and enemies at night, you know, because they try to go in and throw grenades at you; they would, you know, if…if they had enough ammunition, they would ambush you when you left your base. So, you never knew who was the enemy.

<citation>Guadalupe Carrasco, interview by Kanisorn Wongsrichanalai, "War Stories: West Texans and the Experience of War, World War I to the Present," West Texas Collection, Angelo State University, June 25, 2015.</citation>
Casey Blitt was drafted into the army and served as a doctor during the war. He earned a Bronze Star award for his service.

Did some of us have post-traumatic stress disorder? Probably.…I said, that's the worst year of my life.…And everybody says, thank you for your service…and I said, you're very welcome, I said, but it was not voluntary.…I was drafted.…
post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD): a long-term mental health condition caused by extreme stress
<citation>Casey D. Blitt (AFC/2001/001/109053), Transcript, Veterans History Project Collection, American Folklife Center, Library of Congress.</citation>

pieces.text: The following passage describes how the ongoing Vietnam War affected U.S. troop
, meaning spirit, discipline, and confidence. Read the passage. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: U.S. soldiers struggled in difficult, unfamiliar terrain. They fought enemies who often blended in with civilians or disappeared into the jungle after a skirmish. Soldiers were often ordered to take over villages and then told to abandon those same villages after winning the fight. This led some soldiers to question their orders, and the overall purpose of the war.

As the war continued, extremely problematic behaviors became more common. Some soldiers disobeyed orders, lied on battle reports, or left their units without permission. There were even instances of U.S. soldiers attacking Vietnamese civilians.

When veterans returned to the U.S. after serving in Vietnam, they often faced criticism. Some people blamed soldiers for how poorly the war was going, rather than recognizing the failures of the U.S. government. This lack of public support for veterans discouraged many soldiers who were still serving.

contents.text: North Vietnam's 1968 Tet Offensive had major political consequences in the United States. Read the passage. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: In February 1968, about a month into the Tet Offensive, a trusted American journalist said the United States was unable to win in Vietnam. Shortly after that broadcast, President Johnson's approval rating began to fall. His advisors, most of whom had previously supported the war, told him to seek peace.

At the end of March 1968, Johnson went on national television to announce an end to bombing in North Vietnam and to call for peace talks. Based on his rapidly declining popularity, he also withdrew from the 1968 presidential election. This shocked the nation. In November, Richard Nixon, who promised to end the Vietnam War, won the presidential election by defeating Johnson's vice president, Hubert Humphrey.

pieces.text: The following passage describes how the ongoing Vietnam War affected U.S. troop
, meaning spirit, discipline, and confidence. Read the passage. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: U.S. soldiers struggled in difficult, unfamiliar terrain. They fought enemies who often blended in with civilians or disappeared into the jungle after a skirmish. Soldiers were often ordered to take over villages and then told to abandon those same villages after winning the fight. This led some soldiers to question their orders, and the overall purpose of the war.

As the war continued, extremely problematic behaviors became more common. Some soldiers disobeyed orders, lied on battle reports, or left their units without permission. There were even instances of U.S. soldiers attacking Vietnamese civilians.

When veterans returned to the U.S. after serving in Vietnam, they often faced criticism. Some people blamed soldiers for how poorly the war was going, rather than recognizing the failures of the U.S. government. This lack of public support for veterans discouraged many soldiers who were still serving.

choices.text: Troop morale decreased because of challenging fighting conditions.

Soldiers maintained great confidence in U.S. military strategy throughout the war.
Many soldiers were discouraged by criticism of veterans from the American public.

contents.text: After the Tet Offensive, people in the U.S. became increasingly critical of the war. During the 1968 U.S. presidential campaign, Richard Nixon promised "an honorable end to the war in Vietnam." As president, he decided South Vietnam, not the United States, would lead the war effort against North Vietnam. But U.S. forces continued fighting in Vietnam for several more years. The fighting even spread to the neighboring countries of Cambodia and Laos.
Match each military action during Nixon's presidency with its outcome.

draggableItems.text: Communist Cambodian forces suffer a short-term defeat but gain greater political support after the brutal fighting.
By the end of 1972, the U.S. government ends the draft. The U.S. military becomes a smaller, higher-paid, and all-volunteer force.
By the end of 1970, U.S. forces in Vietnam decrease to around 300,000 troops, while South Vietnam's military increases to around 1,000,000 troops.
Even though North Vietnam loses many troops at first, it launches a counterattack that captures or kills half of South Vietnam's invading forces.

staticItems.text: With U.S. air support, South Vietnam's army invades Laos and attacks the Ho Chi Minh Trail, North Vietnam's main supply route into the South.
The U.S. government announces it will begin withdrawing U.S. troops from Vietnam. At the same time, the U.S. will help train and equip South Vietnam's military.
Seeing that the draft was unpopular with soldiers and the public, President Nixon instructs the government to find other ways to maintain a military force.
U.S. and South Vietnamese troops invade Cambodia to fight communist forces threatening its pro-U.S. government.

pieces.text: The following passage describes how the ongoing Vietnam War affected U.S. troop
, meaning spirit, discipline, and confidence. Read the passage. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: U.S. soldiers struggled in difficult, unfamiliar terrain. They fought enemies who often blended in with civilians or disappeared into the jungle after a skirmish. Soldiers were often ordered to take over villages and then told to abandon those same villages after winning the fight. This led some soldiers to question their orders, and the overall purpose of the war.

As the war continued, extremely problematic behaviors became more common. Some soldiers disobeyed orders, lied on battle reports, or left their units without permission. There were even instances of U.S. soldiers attacking Vietnamese civilians.

When veterans returned to the U.S. after serving in Vietnam, they often faced criticism. Some people blamed soldiers for how poorly the war was going, rather than recognizing the failures of the U.S. government. This lack of public support for veterans discouraged many soldiers who were still serving.

contents.text: North Vietnam's 1968 Tet Offensive had major political consequences in the United States. Read the passage. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: In February 1968, about a month into the Tet Offensive, a trusted American journalist said the United States was unable to win in Vietnam. Shortly after that broadcast, President Johnson's approval rating began to fall. His advisors, most of whom had previously supported the war, told him to seek peace.

At the end of March 1968, Johnson went on national television to announce an end to bombing in North Vietnam and to call for peace talks. Based on his rapidly declining popularity, he also withdrew from the 1968 presidential election. This shocked the nation. In November, Richard Nixon, who promised to end the Vietnam War, won the presidential election by defeating Johnson's vice president, Hubert Humphrey.

contents.text: U.S. soldiers faced difficult conditions in Vietnam. The excerpts below come from interviews with two soldiers about their wartime experiences. Read the excerpts or use the audio button to hear recordings from the interviews. Then answer the question below.

pieces.text: Guadalupe Carrasco was drafted into the army and served in a light infantry unit during the war. He earned a Purple Heart award for his service.

content.text: The North Vietnamese Army—they were a regular army, and you knew that they were the enemy. Now the Viet Cong, on the other hand, are farmers during the day and enemies at night, you know, because they try to go in and throw grenades at you; they would, you know, if…if they had enough ammunition, they would ambush you when you left your base. So, you never knew who was the enemy.

<citation>Guadalupe Carrasco, interview by Kanisorn Wongsrichanalai, "War Stories: West Texans and the Experience of War, World War I to the Present," West Texas Collection, Angelo State University, June 25, 2015.</citation>
Casey Blitt was drafted into the army and served as a doctor during the war. He earned a Bronze Star award for his service.

Did some of us have post-traumatic stress disorder? Probably.…I said, that's the worst year of my life.…And everybody says, thank you for your service…and I said, you're very welcome, I said, but it was not voluntary.…I was drafted.…
post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD): a long-term mental health condition caused by extreme stress
<citation>Casey D. Blitt (AFC/2001/001/109053), Transcript, Veterans History Project Collection, American Folklife Center, Library of Congress.</citation>
